Modern.tagline: From the UNESCO town that makes watches.
Modern.brandNameRationale: Picked over Glashütte Manufaktur (A flagged Glashütte Original trademark conflict, even with the Manufaktur variation it sits too close) and Co-Axial Timepieces (the co-axial escapement is associated specifically with Omega in commercial use). Le Locle is a UNESCO World Heritage town (with La Chaux-de-Fonds), recognized in 2009 specifically for watchmaking urban planning, and is in the public domain as a geographic indicator. Le Locle Watches is the safest and the most credible — an accessible Swiss heritage brand rooted in a real, named, UNESCO-recognized watchmaking town.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern accessible Swiss watches in 2025+ sit between Tissot/Mido (Swatch Group entry-Swiss) and the Christopher Ward / Farer indie-Swiss tier. The opening is for a brand that owns a single specific Swiss heritage town — Le Locle — at an accessible price point.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Christopher Ward (christopherward.com) holds the indie-Swiss-value slot. Farer (farer.com) plays the design-led indie peer. Tissot (tissot.ch) is the heritage-accessible benchmark (and is itself headquartered in Le Locle). We sit closest to Christopher Ward with a town-specific identity built around Le Locle.
Modern.positioningStatement: Accessible Swiss watches from the UNESCO watchmaking town.

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark — Le Locle in a precise neo-grotesk, two words on one line, with Watches in small caps below. A small geometric mark — the silhouette of Le Locle's grid plan (the UNESCO inscription cites the rectilinear urban layout designed around watchmaking) — sits as the hallmark.

Luxury.tagline: Certified by the strictest seal in watchmaking.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: Picked over Maison Breguet d'Horlogerie (A correctly flagged Breguet trademark) and Harrison Marine Chronometers. The Poinçon de Genève (Geneva Seal, established 1886) is the strictest finishing certification in watchmaking, administered by the Canton of Geneva — a public certification mark, not a brand. A brand structured around certifying every piece to Geneva Seal standards is uniquely defensible. Harrison is great but marine-specific and narrower. Breguet was correctly flagged as Swatch Group property.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury haute horlogerie above $20,000 is dominated by Patek, AP, Vacheron, Lange. The Geneva Seal is the single most respected finishing certification — fewer than ten brands have ever achieved it. The opening is for a small brand that certifies every piece to Geneva Seal and competes purely on finishing quality.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Roger Dubuis (rogerdubuis.com) certifies every movement to Geneva Seal — the closest direct peer. Vacheron Constantin (vacheron-constantin.com) holds the establishment-haute-horlogerie slot. Patek Philippe (patek.com) is the global benchmark. We sit closer to Roger Dubuis as a Geneva-Seal-only house.
Luxury.positioningStatement: Haute horlogerie certified to Geneva Seal on every piece.

Minimal.tagline: The heart of every mechanical watch.
Minimal.brandNameRationale: Picked over Tourbillon. and Timepiece Studio. Escapement is the most defensibly minimal — every mechanical watch has an escapement, and the word names the single mechanism that makes the watch tick. Tourbillon. is striking but tourbillons are a single (expensive) complication and the brand is too narrow. Timepiece Studio is generic. Escapement names the mechanism that defines the category and is one word.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimalist mechanical watch brands have a real opening for the buyer who wants the movement to be the brand — the visible balance wheel, the open dial, the escapement on display. The opening is for a brand whose name is the mechanism.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Nomos Glashütte (nomos-glashuette.com) sets the design-led minimalist Swiss benchmark. Ressence (ressence.eu) plays the mechanism-led design slot. Anordain (anordain.com) is the Glasgow craft-minimalist peer. We sit between Nomos and Ressence, mechanism-led, single-catalogue.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A minimalist mechanical watch brand named for its defining mechanism.

Corporate.tagline: A portfolio rooted in the Jura watchmaking arc.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Picked over Chronometry Standards Institute and Vallée de Joux Manufactures. The Jura arc (Vallée de Joux, Le Locle, La Chaux-de-Fonds) is the historical watchmaking geography of Switzerland and is in the public domain as a regional identifier. Jura Horological Group is the cleanest holding-company framing. Chronometry Standards Institute is a fine B2B brand but reads more certification body than holding company. Vallée de Joux Manufactures is more specific but overlaps with active makers (AP, JLC) located there. Jura is broader and safer.
Corporate.industrySummary: Holding-company watchmaking groups (Swatch, Richemont, LVMH) own the major maisons. The opening is for a mid-tier holding company that consolidates independent Swiss brands and movement workshops across the Jura arc — a smaller, regional portfolio.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Swatch Group (swatchgroup.com) is the benchmark. Richemont (richemont.com) holds the luxury portfolio slot. Citizen Watch Co (citizenwatch-global.com) plays the Japanese horological group peer. We sit smaller, regional, Jura-arc-specific.
Corporate.positioningStatement: A regional Swiss watchmaking holding group anchored in the Jura arc.

Creative.tagline: One master, one apprentice, twelve watches a year.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Picked over The Régulateur and Anchor & Balance. George Daniels (inventor of the co-axial escapement) and his apprentice Roger Smith represent the most famous master-apprentice lineage in independent English watchmaking — and the model (one master, one apprentice, hand-finishing) is uniquely defensible as a creative brand structure. The Régulateur is a beautiful single-format brand but narrower. Anchor & Balance is good but reads as a generic mechanism-pair. Daniels & Apprentice is the most creative and the most lineage-rooted.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative independent watchmaking has a real opening in the master-apprentice model — Roger Smith's annual output of fewer than ten watches commands six-figure waitlists. The opening is for a brand structured around the master-apprentice lineage and a tiny annual output.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Roger W. Smith (rwsmithwatches.com) is the direct lineage holder and global benchmark for English independent watchmaking. Struthers (struthers.london) plays the London-craft peer. F.P. Journe (fpjourne.com) holds the global haute independent slot. We sit alongside Struthers, master-apprentice English tradition.
Creative.positioningStatement: An independent watchmaker structured around the master-apprentice lineage.
